title: US and Denmark Make a Deal About Greenland
summary:
Greenland is a huge island in the Arctic. It belongs to Denmark, but it governs itself. For months, President Donald Trump said he wanted the US to take Greenland. He said it matters for military defense and has valuable minerals.

That made a lot of people upset. Greenlanders protested in their capital, Nuuk. Denmark and other Nato countries said no.

Now, the US and Denmark have announced a deal. Trump says Denmark will give the US "permanent control over security, and all other needs" in Greenland. He says no US adversary could have a military base there or make sensitive investments without US approval.

Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen welcomed the deal. They say it strengthens security in the Arctic and recognizes Greenland's right to self-determination — that means Greenlanders get to decide their own future.

Nato also welcomed the deal, saying it will help stability in the region. French President Emmanuel Macron said Danish sovereignty — Denmark's control over its own territory — is respected.

No one has released the actual text of the agreement yet. It is expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week. After that, parliaments still have to approve it.
why_it_matters: It shows how countries can disagree strongly about land and still work out a deal — and that the people who live in a place want a say in what happens to it.

background_read: Greenland is the world's largest island, and most of it is covered in thick ice. It belongs to Denmark (a country in northern Europe), but Greenland has its own government that runs most of the island's daily business.
In 2019, Donald Trump (the current U.S. president) suggested the United States might buy Greenland, and Denmark said no.
Nato (a group of countries that promise to defend each other) watches the Arctic closely, because it sits between the United States and Russia.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump, Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen, Nato, and French President Emmanuel Macron.
WHAT: The US and Denmark announced a deal giving the US 'permanent control over security, and all other needs' in Greenland, but the actual text has not been released.
WHERE: Greenland, a huge Arctic island that belongs to Denmark, with protests in its capital, Nuuk, and a signing expected at the UN General Assembly.
WHY: The US wants Greenland for military defense and valuable minerals, while Denmark and Greenland insist that Greenlanders decide their own future.

perspectives.description: Trump says the deal means no US adversary could build a military base in Greenland or make sensitive investments there without US approval.
Greenland's prime minister welcomes the deal because it recognizes self-determination — the right of Greenlanders to decide their own future.
Nobody has seen the actual text of the agreement yet, and parliaments still have to approve it, so the details could still change.
